title: Restricted internal scalar extension equals relative tensor, naturally
statement:
Let $C$ be an essentially small site, and let $H=\operatorname{Sh}(C,\operatorname{Ab})$ have the canonical sheafified tensor over $\mathbf Z$, with sheafification and closed symmetric monoidal structure as in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor]. Use internal module objects [sk-def-sfb-module-objects] and the coequalizer relative tensor and its induced monoidal structure [def-sfb-modobj-relative-tensor]. For any commutative ring object $R$, write $U:\operatorname{Mod}_R(H)\to H$ for the forgetful functor and $t_{P,M}:UP\otimes UM\to U(P\otimes_R M)$ for the canonical coequalizer projection.
Let $\varphi:R\to B$ be a morphism of commutative ring objects, let $N=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(B)$ be the restricted regular module, and use scalar extension and restriction of [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Put $E(M)=\operatorname{Res}_\varphi(\operatorname{Ext}_\varphi M)$ and let $p_M:B\otimes UM\to UE(M)$ be the scalar-extension coequalizer projection. There is a natural isomorphism of $R$-module valued functors
$$\kappa:E\xrightarrow{\sim}N\otimes_R-$$
whose components satisfy, as morphisms in $H$,
$$U(\kappa_M)\circ p_M=t_{N,M},\qquad U(\kappa_M^{-1})\circ t_{N,M}=p_M.$$
In particular both components are $R$-linear and mutually inverse. Explicitly its naturality says that for every $R$-linear map $f:M\to M'$, one has
$$\kappa_{M'}\circ E(f)=(\operatorname{id}_N\otimes_R f)\circ\kappa_M.$$
No freeness hypothesis on $B$ over $R$ is imposed, and these equations are identities of sheaf morphisms, not an identification of tensor-sheaf sections with sectionwise tensor products.
